title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends 14 Quick-Commerce Licences in Sweeping Food Safety Crackdown
excerpt: Inspections at Blinkit, Zepto, and Instamart dark stores found cockroaches, rotten food, and rodent droppings as FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe expands his enforcement drive.
body:
• Maharashtra FDA suspended 14 food business licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart dark stores after inspecting 86 establishments across the state
  • Inspectors found cockroach infestations, rotten vegetables, rodent droppings, rusted storage racks, and missing medical records at multiple facilities
  • The crackdown, led by FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, has expanded to Domino's and Pizza Hut outlets, elite Mumbai clubs, and popular eateries

Statewide Raids Target Quick-Commerce Dark Stores

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended 14 food business licences after a statewide inspection drive targeting quick-commerce and online food delivery platforms, including Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart.

The special drive, conducted on August 13, covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale, and delivery of food through online platforms. In addition to the 14 licence suspensions, regulators ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations and issued 60 improvement notices, according to IANS.

Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit (operated by Eternal's Blink Commerce), five to Zepto, and two to Instamart. The remaining two licences belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta ENT Pvt. Ltd.

What Inspectors Found

Inspection reports paint a grim picture of food storage conditions at some of India's biggest quick-commerce operations.

A Blink Commerce facility in Mumbai's Ghatkopar scored 34 out of 74 (46%) on the FDA's compliance checklist and was classified as non-compliant. Inspectors found dirty storage racks, poor segregation of food and non-food items, rotten vegetables, and cockroach infestations. The facility also had damaged flooring and ceilings, and records related to medical examinations and drinking-water testing were missing.

A RAJIDI Retail facility in Bandra West scored 60 out of 136 (45%). The FDA documented dust, cobwebs, food waste, and significant rodent droppings. Rusted racks, damaged flooring, and inadequate segregation were also observed.

At a Zepto warehouse in Nashik, delivery staff were entering storage areas in street footwear, raising cross-contamination risks, according to the FDA statement reported by Reuters.

\"We will not tolerate any playing with public health.\"

— Tukaram Mundhe, Maharashtra FDA Commissioner

A Broader Crackdown Gaining Momentum

The quick-commerce raids are part of a sweeping food safety drive led by Maharashtra's new FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, 51, who has become something of a social media sensation for his aggressive enforcement approach.

In recent weeks, Mundhe's department has shut four Domino's outlets and one Pizza Hut location in Maharashtra after finding grease residue in pizza-making machines, insect infestations, and products without expiry dates, according to Reuters. The department also suspended FSSAI licences of five elite Mumbai clubs, including the Cricket Club of India (CCI), Willingdon Sports Club, and MIG Cricket Club, after inspections revealed cockroach and fly infestations, expired food items, and fungal growth on vegetables.

Earlier, a Blinkit facility in Mumbai's Malad West had its licence suspended after officials discovered extensive cockroach infestation during an inspection. Karnataka's food safety department followed suit, sealing a major Zepto warehouse in Bengaluru's Hoskote for similar violations.

The Scale of Quick Commerce in India

The raids put a spotlight on a $13 billion sector that processes 9 million daily orders across India. As of June 2026, Blinkit operated 2,443 active dark stores across 300 cities, Swiggy Instamart ran 1,171 stores across 131 cities, and Zepto had 1,139 stores across 66 cities, according to Inc42.

The Indian government told Parliament that over 5.1 lakh consumer complaints were registered against e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms on the National Consumer Helpline in 2025 alone, with Zepto logging 5,774 complaints and Blinkit 5,102.

What It Means for Consumers

Maharashtra now requires e-commerce food delivery companies to obtain state approval before opening new dark stores and mandates inspections of these facilities every six months. The state has also expanded FDA staffing and increased the number of food testing laboratories to strengthen enforcement.

For consumers who rely on quick-commerce platforms for groceries, the crackdown is a reminder that the speed and convenience of 10-minute delivery can come at a cost when storage conditions are compromised. Swiggy, Eternal, and Zepto have so far declined to comment publicly on the findings.
